Senses.PreferredTarget: an attached comment on a case
Senses.Explanation: An attached comment is a short remark fixed to a case, one line of dialogue, or a verse; verbal constructions describe attaching that same comment. The headword occurs 327 times in 120 allowlisted texts. The Blue Cliff Record directly says, “in the assembly this is called an attached comment” (眾中謂之著語), and elsewhere, “this is called an attached comment” (此謂之著語). Xuedou Chongxian attaches a comment and then gives its words; records also specify the exact point where Xuedou or Dahui Zonggao comments, such as at the words “do not think falsely” or at the point of stepping down. Baishan Dekai is asked to attach comments to a set of twelve questions. Chan makes the comment and its precise attachment a formal device of case commentary rather than generic speech. The act and resulting words are grammatical views of one commentarial object and remain one sense.
Senses.Note: The former operation/product targets were not distinguishable as different referents from their glosses alone: both name the same attached comment. Keep it distinct from laying down a response (下語), answering in another's place (代語), extended appraisal-commentary (評唱), and a verse on an old case (頌古).
